item.title: Calf / Posterior Leg MFR
clinicalUse: Adjunct for dorsiflexion limitation when calf sensitivity contributes
patientPosition: Prone or supine with knee supported.
contact: Broad palm/forearm or cross-hand contact over gastrocnemius/soleus, avoiding popliteal fossa.
forceDirection: Slow longitudinal or cross-hand load along posterior calf.
safety: Never treat suspected DVT; avoid acute tear/hematoma.
item.visualCue: Broad calf contact → Slow fascial load → Re-test dorsiflexion/calf function.

subTechniques.name: Calf Myofascial Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve comfortable dorsiflexion and calf movement tolerance when myofascial restriction is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone or supine with the ankle free and the calf fully supported.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over gastrocnemius/soleus muscle bellies, avoiding deep pressure in the popliteal fossa.
subTechniques.direction: Sustain a gentle longitudinal or oblique fascial load; ankle movement may be added slowly if it remains comfortable.
subTechniques.reassess: Weight-bearing dorsiflexion, gait and calf raise.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: A calf technique should never substitute for screening unexplained swelling or vascular symptoms.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Do not apply when DVT is suspected.

subTechniques.name: Plantar Fascial / Intrinsic Foot Release
subTechniques.target: Plantar fascia and intrinsic foot soft tissue
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve local plantar soft-tissue comfort and foot-loading tolerance.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine or sitting with the foot supported.
subTechniques.contact: Thumb or broad knuckle contact along the plantar soft tissue, avoiding excessive focal pressure at the heel.
subTechniques.direction: Use slow longitudinal or transverse tissue loading; combine with gentle toe extension only if comfortable.
subTechniques.dosage: 30–90 seconds per area, followed by active foot loading.
subTechniques.reassess: First-step pain, toe extension and walking tolerance.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Follow manual work with calf/foot strengthening and graded loading rather than relying on tissue pressure alone.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid open skin, acute bruising or severe sensory loss.
